svg.aria-label: Monthly cost against hours per day. Oracle's Enhanced cluster fee of $74.40 a month is fixed, so its line starts above zero: scaling the node pool to zero still bills that floor, and only destroying the cluster reaches zero. Civo's control plane is free, so its line passes through the origin. At 24 by 7 Oracle costs $286 and Civo $261.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
text.tspan: · and why part of it does not switch off

svg.text: Oracle figures are the official Cost Estimator breakdown for the reference cluster. Civo is compute only — its control plane is free. PVC volumes bill separately in both.

svg.text: On an Enhanced cluster, scaling the pool to 0 does not reach $0

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: cluster-down.sh removes the $212/mo of nodes and boot volumes, but leaves the $74.40/mo cluster fee running. Between sessions that is the difference between ~$74/mo and $0.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Oracle suspends the pool, so PVC data survives a down/up. Civo has no stop — its off switch is terraform destroy, and PVC data goes with it unless the volumes use Retain.
